cpu: Intel Core i9-14900K (8 P-cores with hyper-threading + 16 E-cores, 32 threads, AVX2 + FMA, no AVX-512)
notes: statevector.csv: best of 16 or 32 threads for each simulator; qvd includes allocating the state, the others include sampling one shot, and qsim includes converting the circuit in Python.

stabilizer.csv: rotated surface code memory experiments with d rounds; qvd on a pool of 8 P-cores or 1 thread; Stim is single-threaded. A virtual machine shared the machine: Stim, Aer and qvd on 1 thread ran while it used about six cores; qvd on 8 P-cores was re-measured after the parallel reference shot while it used about 14.

stabilizer_steps.csv: distance-101 surface code, 101 rounds; the conditions column says whether the machine was quiet or shared with the virtual machine (step 8; under that load the step-7 build took 2.57 s). Steps 1-6 used a generator that measured each ancilla right after its closing H.
